alert.title: Supply6 just launched a SILT Nights rival
alert.text: Supply6 Mellow launched on 18 Oct 2026 (about ₹45 a serving, on Blinkit and Zepto), and its Meta ads in India started around 5 Nov: 11 ads so far. It is a nightly sachet with L-Theanine, L-Glycine, Magnesium and KSM-66 Ashwagandha, "zero melatonin". That is nearly the SILT Nights formula, at lower doses (1.25 g glycine against SILT's 3 g, 150 mg KSM-66 against 300 mg). Their headline: "Body tired. Brain still at work." The ads are 12 days old, so nothing has proven itself yet. Track them weekly. SILT's openings: every dose printed and compared with the dose used in studies, magnesium bisglycinate named as the form, a lab report per ingredient, and a Morning + Night system instead of one more product in a 6-SKU catalogue.

patterns.title: Creators beat studio ads
patterns.text: 10 of the 15 longest-running videos are a creator talking to a phone camera. 85 of 230 ads carry a creator tag (#ad, @supply6), so most of their spend runs as partnership ads through creator handles.

patterns.title: The symptom comes first, the product after 10 to 15 seconds
patterns.text: Hooks name a feeling the viewer has today: "I'm tired all the time", "your alarm goes off and you're already exhausted", "brain fog could be low B12", "bloated after every meal". The product is the answer, never the opener.

patterns.title: One hard number for proof
patterns.text: The same two numbers appear everywhere: "raises B12 by 92% and D3 by 67%", plus "63+ nutrients" and "3 billion CFU". The stat sits late in the script, after the problem lands.

patterns.title: "One sachet replaces your shelf"
patterns.text: Simplicity is the core promise. "How many supplements do you take? Just this one." "No complicated routine, no multiple supplements." Their 360 product gets 76 of 230 ads.

patterns.title: Offers carry the statics
patterns.text: The welcome kit (60 days + free glass bottle and frother, "worth ₹1000") is their biggest bet: 36 ads, 97 versions, 51 images. Salts statics run on a 15% code. They also anchor price per day ("₹72 a day").

patterns.title: Hindi and Hinglish versions
patterns.text: 4 of the top 15 are Hindi or Hinglish, with cruder, funnier hooks ("You rely on these two to poop?"). They test the same message in two languages.
